*Last updated November 2026.*

This textbook site, geog215.org, asks students in GEOG 215 to sign in so it can show you your own progress and so your instructor can see which topics the class finds hard. To do that, the site stores your name and email address on a secure server, along with a record of how you use the textbook. This page explains what is stored, who can see it, how it is protected, and your choices.

## What the site stores

| Information | Details |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Name and email address | Taken from the class roster by your instructor. Your email is how you sign in. |
| Course and term | For example, GEOG 215, Spring 2027, plus an optional note such as your section. |
| Sign-in account | An account with your email address, when it was created, and when you last signed in. The sign-in service also keeps short-term security logs (such as IP address and browser type) to prevent abuse. |
| Pages you open | Which textbook pages you visit, how many times, and when you first and last opened each one. |
| Practice questions | Your answers to the "check your understanding" questions: your latest answer, the number of attempts, and whether you got it right. |
| Practice code | The R code you run in the textbook's code boxes (the latest version only, up to 4,000 characters), how many times you ran it, and whether it produced an error. |
| Chapter practice quizzes | How many questions you answered right and wrong, practice points and streaks, and whether you finished the quiz. |
| Feedback and Discussion Questions | Some survey feedback and/or discussion questions may be stored on this site. These are not used in grading, but to provide feedback. |

## What the site does not store

- **Your grades.** No course grades, assignment scores, exam results, or feedback are stored on geog215.org. Grades are kept only in the university's systems (Canvas and Gradescope).
- **Practice quiz points are not grades.** The points on the chapter practice quizzes are for your own practice. They do not count toward your course grade and are not used to decide it.
- **Passwords.** The site has no passwords. You sign in with a one-time code or link sent to your email. Your Onyen and Onyen password are never requested or stored.
- Your PID, date of birth, address, phone number, Social Security number, or any financial information.

## Why the information is used

- To let only students in the course sign in to the textbook.
- To let you pick up where you left off and see your own progress.
- To help your instructor see which pages, questions, and code exercises students find difficult, so the course and textbook can be improved.

Your information is never sold, never used for advertising, and never used to calculate your grade. It will not be used for research or publication unless you agree in a separate, approved research consent form.

## Who can see it

- **You.** When signed in, you can only see your own records. Other students cannot see your name, email, or activity.
- **Your instructor.** The instructor can view the class roster and activity on a protected admin page and can download it as a spreadsheet for course purposes. Instructors can only see the courses they are assigned to.
- **Service providers.** The companies below run the site on the course's behalf. They handle your information only to provide their service.

| Provider | What it does | What it receives |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| [Supabase](https://supabase.com/privacy) | Database and sign-in service. Servers are in the United States (US East). | Everything listed under "What the site stores". |
| [Resend](https://resend.com/legal/privacy-policy) | Delivers the sign-in emails from mail.geog215.org. | Your email address and the sign-in email. |
| [Cloudflare](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/) | Hosts the website and delivers its pages. | Standard web request data, such as IP address and browser type. |
| [jsDelivr](https://www.jsdelivr.com/terms/privacy-policy-jsdelivr-net) | Delivers the sign-in software library to your browser. | Standard web request data. |
| [Google Analytics](https://policies.google.com/privacy) | Measures overall site traffic (pages viewed, device type, approximate location) using cookies. | Usage data that is not linked to your name or email. |

The R code you run in the textbook runs inside your own web browser, not on a server. Only the information listed under "What the site stores" is sent to the database.

## How the information is protected

- **Encrypted in transit.** All connections to geog215.org, the database, and the email service use HTTPS/TLS encryption.
- **Encrypted at rest.** Supabase, the database provider, documents that stored data is encrypted at rest (AES-256).
- **Row-level security.** The database enforces access rules on every table. The class roster cannot be read from any web browser at all, and each student can read only their own activity.
- **Restricted sign-in.** Only email addresses on the class roster (and approved instructors) can create an account. The admin page checks that the person is an approved instructor before showing anything.
- **No passwords to steal.** One-time sign-in codes expire after use, so no passwords are stored.
- **Access can be removed.** The instructor can turn off a student's access at any time, for example when a student drops the course.

## How long it is kept

Your information is kept for the semester you are enrolled and is deleted no later than **12 months** after the semester ends, unless you ask for it to be deleted sooner. Deleting your record removes your roster entry, all of your activity for that course and term, and your sign-in account if you are not enrolled in another course that uses the site.

## Your choices and rights

- **Taking part is voluntary.** Saying no will not affect your grade or your standing in the course in any way.
- **You can use the textbook without signing in.** The same textbook chapters are available as an static PDF on the Canvas site, which does not ask for your name or email and does not save your progress. Course announcements, assignments, and deadlines are always on Canvas.
- **You can change your mind.** You can withdraw your consent at any time by emailing your instructor. Your access will be turned off and your information deleted.
- **You can see, correct, or delete your information.** Email your instructor to get a copy of what is stored about you, to correct it, or to have it deleted.
- **You can limit analytics.** You can block or delete cookies in your browser, or use [Google's opt-out tool](https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout), without losing access to the textbook.

## FERPA

Your name, email address, enrollment, and the activity records described above are education records protected by the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA). They are used only for this course, shared only with course staff and the service providers that run the site on the course's behalf, and are not disclosed to anyone else without your written consent except as FERPA allows. You also have the right to inspect your education records and to ask for corrections. For more about your FERPA rights, see the [UNC Office of the University Registrar](https://registrar.unc.edu/).

## Questions and changes

Questions about this policy or your information: contact your instructor, **David Parr**, at [daveparr\@unc.edu](mailto:daveparr@unc.edu){.email}. If this policy changes in a way that affects how your information is used, you will be told and asked for your consent again.
